tools.name: preview_deposit_charges_for_no_shows
tools.description: Looks up reservations for a date that were marked as no-shows and charges each guest's card the no-show fee through Stripe. Returns a summary of the charges made and any that failed.

params.name: fee_cents_per_guest
params.description: No-show fee per guest in cents

tools.code:
import sqlite3

import stripe

DATABASE_PATH = "reservations.db"
stripe.api_key = "sk_live_configured_elsewhere"


def preview_deposit_charges_for_no_shows(service_date: str, fee_cents_per_guest: int = 2500) -> dict:
    connection = sqlite3.connect(DATABASE_PATH)
    connection.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    try:
        no_show_rows = connection.execute(
            "SELECT id, guest_name, party_size, stripe_customer_id, stripe_payment_method_id "
            "FROM reservations WHERE reservation_date = ? AND status = 'no_show'",
            (service_date,),
        ).fetchall()
    finally:
        connection.close()

    result = {"service_date": service_date, "charged": [], "failed": [], "skipped": [], "total_cents": 0}

    for row in no_show_rows:
        if not row["stripe_customer_id"] or not row["stripe_payment_method_id"]:
            result["skipped"].append({"reservation_id": row["id"], "reason": "no card on file"})
            continue
        amount_cents = fee_cents_per_guest * row["party_size"]
        try:
            payment_intent = stripe.PaymentIntent.create(
                amount=amount_cents,
                currency="usd",
                customer=row["stripe_customer_id"],
                payment_method=row["stripe_payment_method_id"],
                off_session=True,
                confirm=True,
                description="No-show fee for reservation " + str(row["id"]),
                idempotency_key="noshow-" + str(row["id"]) + "-" + service_date,
            )
            result["charged"].append(
                {"reservation_id": row["id"], "guest": row["guest_name"], "amount_cents": amount_cents, "payment_intent": payment_intent.id}
            )
            result["total_cents"] += amount_cents
        except stripe.error.StripeError as stripe_error:
            result["failed"].append({"reservation_id": row["id"], "error": str(stripe_error)})

    result["charged_count"] = len(result["charged"])
    result["failed_count"] = len(result["failed"])
    return result

tools.name: invite_guest_to_manage_reservation
tools.description: Gives a guest a management link and edit access to their reservation, saves the access token on the reservation, and emails the link to the guest.

params.name: guest_email
params.description: Email address to send the link to

tools.code:
import secrets
import smtplib
import sqlite3
from email.message import EmailMessage

DATABASE_PATH = "reservations.db"
SMTP_HOST = "smtp.restaurant.example"
SENDER_ADDRESS = "reservations@restaurant.example"
MANAGE_BASE_URL = "https://restaurant.example/manage/"


def invite_guest_to_manage_reservation(reservation_id: int, guest_email: str) -> str:
    generated_access_token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
    database_connection = sqlite3.connect(DATABASE_PATH)
    try:
        update_cursor = database_connection.execute(
            "UPDATE reservations SET manage_token = ?, guest_can_edit = 1, guest_email = ? WHERE id = ?",
            (generated_access_token, guest_email, reservation_id),
        )
        database_connection.commit()
        if update_cursor.rowcount == 0:
            return "Reservation not found"
    finally:
        database_connection.close()

    invitation_message = EmailMessage()
    invitation_message["From"] = SENDER_ADDRESS
    invitation_message["To"] = guest_email
    invitation_message["Subject"] = "Manage your reservation"
    invitation_message.set_content("You can change or review your reservation here: " + MANAGE_BASE_URL + generated_access_token)

    with smtplib.SMTP(SMTP_HOST, 587) as smtp_connection:
        smtp_connection.starttls()
        smtp_connection.send_message(invitation_message)

    return "Management link sent to " + guest_email

tools.name: check_availability_with_sync
tools.description: Looks up open tables for a date, time and party size, and triggers the floor plan sync job so the availability is current.
tools.code:
import sqlite3
import subprocess
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP

mcp = FastMCP("reservations")

DATABASE_PATH = "reservations.db"


@dataclass
class AvailabilityResult:
    service_date: str
    party_size: int
    sync_ok: bool
    open_table_ids: list = field(default_factory=list)


@mcp.tool()
def check_availability_with_sync(service_date: str, party_size: int) -> AvailabilityResult:
    sync_process = subprocess.run(
        ["python", "scripts/sync_floor_plan.py", "--date", service_date],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=30,
    )
    connection = sqlite3.connect(DATABASE_PATH)
    try:
        rows = connection.execute(
            "SELECT t.id FROM tables t WHERE t.seats >= ? AND t.id NOT IN "
            "(SELECT table_id FROM reservations WHERE reservation_date = ? AND table_id IS NOT NULL AND status != 'cancelled') "
            "ORDER BY t.seats",
            (party_size, service_date),
        ).fetchall()
    finally:
        connection.close()
    return AvailabilityResult(
        service_date=service_date,
        party_size=party_size,
        sync_ok=sync_process.returncode == 0,
        open_table_ids=[row[0] for row in rows],
    )
